name: Tainted Memorandum
summary: In Coldridge Valley, Sten Stoutarm quietly sends you to Alamar Grimm in Anvilmar. Grimm urges you to trust dark power over your dwarven hosts.

sections.title: A Discreet Summons
sections.body: Warlocks face deep suspicion in Coldridge Valley. As you help Sten Stoutarm with local threats, he reluctantly slips you a note. His warning makes plain how little your kind is trusted here, even under the uneasy truce that allows warlocks to practice in Alliance lands.

sections.title: Gnomish Bitterness in Exile
sections.body: In Anvilmar, Alamar Grimm speaks of the gnomes’ plight. He believes ordinary magic and tinkering failed Gnomeregan, bringing their people near extinction and leaving them as second-class refugees dependent on dwarven goodwill. He urges you to trust neither the Holy Light nor dwarven politics. Instead, summon fiends and master them, for their obedience is unconditional.

faq.answer: The Tainted Memorandum is a written message Sten Stoutarm gives novice gnome warlocks in Coldridge Valley. It directs them to seek Alamar Grimm, the warlock trainer in Anvilmar.

faq.q: Why are warlocks distrusted in Coldridge Valley?
faq.answer: Dwarves and their Alliance allies prize martial honor and the Holy Light. They regard demonology and shadow magic as corrupt and dangerous, so gnome warlocks face deep suspicion.

Alamar Grimm is a gnome warlock trainer in Anvilmar. Bitter over Gnomeregan’s fall and the gnomes’ dependence on dwarven charity, he teaches young gnomes to bind demonic minions and claim power for themselves.

faq.q: Why does Grimm criticize normal magic and technology?
faq.answer: Grimm believes conventional engineering and accepted schools of magic failed the gnomes in the disaster at Gnomeregan. He says this left them dependent on dwarf patrons who put ties with humans ahead of reclaiming the gnome homeland.

faq.q: Can dwarf warlocks receive this quest?
faq.answer: No. In Dun Morogh, only gnomes can practice the warlock path, so the summons is for newly arrived gnome practitioners.

faq.q: Where does this quest take place?
faq.answer: You begin near Sten Stoutarm in Coldridge Valley and finish inside Anvilmar, the central redoubt overlooking the valley in southwestern Dun Morogh.

angles.text: As a warlock, you receive a missive marking your formal entry into the craft. It presents demonic pacts as a practical choice born of survival, not madness.
As a gnome, you may share the resentment some exiles feel over losing their home and depending on Ironforge.
As a dwarf, you see your people tolerate these dark practitioners under their roof with obvious distaste and sharp wariness.
